chains.name: CardActionChain
chains.about: Card body click → navigate to detail. addToCart action → move the STAGED qty for this card into the cart (qty from pendingQtyById, display data from the forwarded row or pendingRowById). Preserves the added / already-in / updated notifications.

chains.name: CatalogAddCheckedToCartChain
chains.about: "Add Checked to Cart" — move every selected (staged) item into the cart. Qty comes from pendingQtyById (default 1); display data from pendingRowById. For any selected id whose row wasn't captured (e.g. select-all over a card the user never touched), fetch it by id from the catalog endpoint.

chains.name: CatalogCheckboxChangedChain
chains.about: Checkbox toggle → STAGING only (selectedEquipmentKeys + pendingQtyById). Checking stages qty 1 (or keeps a higher staged qty); unchecking clears the stage — UNLESS the item is already in the cart, in which case we hold the uncheck behind a confirmation dialog (its Yes path removes from the cart).

chains.name: CatalogClearAgreementFilterChain
chains.about: Remove the agreement CATALOG FILTER only — NOT the agreement context. The SDP's agreementId is gated on agreementFilterActive, so flipping this false drops the agreement scope and the user can browse the FULL catalog. The agreement CONTEXT is deliberately preserved: fromAgreementId, requestOrigin, agreementRateByEquipmentId, agreementLineIdByEquipmentId and the request's customerId all stay — so cart lines already added keep their negotiated rates and their 'agreement' origin, and the request still submits as an agreement order. (Re-applying the filter = set this true again.)

chains.name: CatalogClearTemplateFilterChain
chains.about: Clear the active template filter → the catalog SDP drops the templateId uriParameter and re-queries the FULL catalog. Triggered by the custom "Template: <name> ✕" chip in the search slot.

chains.name: CatalogCloneTemplateChain
chains.about: Clone a template -> a NEW template owned by whoever cloned it. This is also what makes the shared templates useful to a normal user. Every one of the 20 pre-existing templates is global and ownerless, so under the rule "manager tier edits what is shared" a normal user can edit none of them. Cloning turns that read-only wall into a working path: take a copy, own it, change it freely. The copy is always PERSONAL -- cloning is not a way to publish. Making it global stays a deliberate, manager-tier act via Edit.

chains.name: CatalogDeleteTemplateChain
chains.about: Remove a template, after its confirm dialog. SOFT delete: PATCH isActiveFlag='N'. Deliberately NOT the deleteRequestTemplate endpoint, which exists and is tempting — a hard DELETE on the header would either fail the EQR_TEMPLATE_LINE foreign key or orphan every line behind it, and it cannot be undone. Switching the flag keeps the rows and is reversible. ENFORCED SERVER-SIDE since backend V477, and verified: the list excludes is_active_flag='N' by default, and both template-lines?templateId= and views/equipment-catalog?templateId= now require the header to be active -- they return EMPTY…

chains.name: CatalogFilterByTemplateChain
chains.about: Clicking a template name FILTERS the catalog to that template's equipment. The filter is driven by activeTemplateId, bound into the catalog SDP's templateId uriParameter — so it re-queries SERVER-SIDE, independent of the smart-search's filterCriterion (which the component owns exclusively; its filter-criterion is read-only write-back and won't ingest an external set). A custom removable chip in the search slot reflects activeTemplateId. This does NOT add anything to the cart. Closes the templates dialog.

chains.name: CatalogFilterCriterionChangedChain
chains.about: Fires on oj-sp-smart-search's own on-filter-criterion-changed — i.e. when the user picks/clears a chip DIRECTLY (not via the sidebar, which has its own chains and already handles all of this). Fixes "Subclass filter not working as expected with the parent class": 1. The Subclass chip's dropdown was NEVER scoped to the selected Class — SubclassOptionsArray (the master list) was bound straight to the chip, unfiltered, so any subclass of any class could be picked regardless of the current Class chip. 2. Nothing reconciled the two chips against each other, so picking a Class after a Subclass (or…

chains.name: CatalogInitChain
chains.about: Everything below runs before the cards are allowed to render — see the catalogReady flip in the finally. The gate is what stops the SDP firing a bare fetch (no dates, no org) the instant the list-view binds, which is both wasted and misleading: the catalog endpoint is date-scoped, so that response is priced from nothing.

chains.name: CatalogOpenDeleteTemplateChain
chains.about: Trash icon on a template row -> stash the target and ask for confirmation. The acting half is CatalogDeleteTemplateChain.

chains.name: CatalogOpenEditTemplateChain
chains.about: Pencil icon on a template row -> seed the edit form and open the dialog. The acting half is CatalogSaveTemplateEditChain (house two-chain split).

chains.name: CatalogOrgChangeCancelChain
chains.about: "Keep current org" on #orgChangeDialog. Nothing was applied — the org, the SDP's rate scope and the cart were all left alone while the dialog was open — so this only has to discard the pending pick and put the CHIP back on the org still in force. Without that last step the chip would keep displaying the org the user just declined, while the page prices from the old one.

chains.name: CatalogOrgChangeConfirmChain
chains.about: THE ONE PLACE an Equipment Requested Org change is applied. Reached two ways, both of which stash the new org on $page.pendingOrgId first (CatalogFilterCriterionChangedChain): • cart EMPTY — called directly, nothing to move, no dialog shown • cart NON-EMPTY — called by the user confirming #orgChangeDialog Why one chain for both: applying an org is four coupled writes (the request object, the draft, the SDP's org param and the chip itself) plus a refetch of the cart. Two copies of that would drift, and the failure mode of drift is a cart sourced from one org while the UI claims another. ONE…

chains.name: CatalogPreviewAddSelectedChain
chains.about: "Add selected to cart" from the template-preview dialog. Takes the checked preview lines and writes them straight into the CART (CartItemsArray) — qty comes from the template line, display data from the row captured at preview time. Mirrors CatalogAddCheckedToCartChain's write pattern. Lines no longer in the catalog (no captured row) are skipped + reported.

chains.name: CatalogPreviewSelectAllChain
chains.about: Select-all toggle for the preview dialog. Selects every AVAILABLE line; if they are all already selected, clears the selection. Lines no longer in the catalog (available === false) are never selectable.

chains.name: CatalogPreviewShowInCatalogChain
chains.about: "Show in catalog" from the preview dialog. Sets activeTemplateId, bound into the catalog SDP's templateId uriParameter — the grid re-queries server-side to show only the template's equipment. A custom removable chip in the search slot reflects it. Closes the preview (and the templates list dialog if open).

chains.name: CatalogPreviewTemplateChain
chains.about: Eye-preview → open the preview dialog showing the template's lines. READ-ONLY: fetches the template's lines lazily (by serverId), enriches each against the catalog (name / class) for display, and lists them with a selection checkbox. No cart writes, no staging — the user reviews here and then either "Add selected to cart" or "Show in catalog".

chains.name: CatalogPreviewToggleChain
chains.about: Toggle a single preview-line checkbox. Maintains previewSelectedKeys (the set of selected equipment master ids) + bumps previewSelectionTick so the native checkboxes re-sync. Selection lives ONLY in the preview dialog — it does not touch the catalog's staging or the cart.

chains.name: CatalogQtyChangedChain
chains.about: Per-card quantity stepper → STAGING only (pendingQtyById). Does NOT touch the cart; the item enters the cart only on an explicit Add action. The checkbox highlight follows the 0 ⇄ positive transition.

chains.name: CatalogSaveTemplateEditChain
chains.about: Save the template edit dialog: name, description and scope. Two things make this more than one PATCH: 1. SCOPE is a privileged change. Only manager tier may publish to GLOBAL, and the check is repeated here because the dialog's gate is cosmetic. 2. EQR_TEMPLATE_LINE carries DENORMALIZED NOT-NULL copies of the header's name and description (the create path has to send them on every line). Renaming the header alone leaves every line holding the old text. So a rename cascades to the lines. Nothing in THIS app reads those columns today, which is exactly why the drift would go unnoticed until a…

chains.name: CatalogSelectAllChain
chains.about: Select All / Deselect All toggle over every row the current filters match. Stages qty 1 for each selected id (no cart change). Deselecting items that are in the cart is gated behind the confirmation dialog. Ids come from the DATA PROVIDER, not the DOM. The previous version read document.querySelectorAll over the rendered cards, which made "Select All" silently mean "select all the rows I have scrolled past" -- with scroll-policy="loadMoreOnScroll" and fetch-size 24, a user who had not scrolled selected 24 of 306 rows and got no indication the rest were missed. Fetching from the provider…

chains.name: CatalogSidebarClassClickChain
chains.about: Class-row click. Toggles expand/collapse + selection (local UI state), then writes the class chip into filterCriterion (DPV re-queries server-side and the chip shows in smart-search). Subclass + "All" clicks route through CatalogSidebarSelectChain.

chains.name: CatalogSidebarSelectChain
chains.about: Sidebar "All Equipment" (empty params → clear class/subclass) and subclass clicks (set class + subclass). Writes the selection INTO filterCriterion as chips so (a) the DPV re-queries the server and (b) the smart-search shows the matching chips — sidebar and chips are one filter state.

chains.name: CatalogTemplateScopeFilterChain
chains.about: Switch the All / Mine / Global tab in the templates dialog. Purely local — the whole visible set is already in templatesArray, so changing tab costs no network call.

chains.name: CatalogTemplateSearchChain
chains.about: Search the templates dialog. The term is kept on a page variable as well as in the DOM input, so a refresh after an edit or delete can re-apply what the user had typed instead of silently resetting their list. Filtering goes through templateScope.filterRows, which applies VISIBILITY first and the search term last. That ordering is the point: a search must never surface a template the user is not allowed to see.

chains.name: CatalogTemplatesChain
chains.about: Opens the Templates dialog. The loading, scoping and filtering all live in CatalogTemplatesRefreshChain so there is exactly one place that decides which templates a user may see. This chain only owns the dialog: reset the search box, open immediately for instant feedback, then let the refresh fill it in behind the spinner. The list is ALWAYS re-fetched on open rather than served from the cache. The old chain cached templatesArray for the page lifetime, which is no longer safe now that templates can be edited and deleted — a stale row would still be clickable, and worse, identity and roles…

chains.name: CatalogTemplatesRefreshChain
chains.about: THE single source of truth for the templates list: load -> project -> decorate -> filter. Every other template chain calls this rather than fetching for itself, so there is one place where scope is applied and one place to fix when it is wrong. Re-run after every mutation. templatesArray is cached for the page lifetime, so an edit or delete that does not refresh leaves the dialog showing the row as it was.

chains.name: DiscardAndGoBackChain
chains.about: Reset the cart (flow variable + localStorage) so the next catalog visit starts empty. CatalogInitChain reads from draftStorage on entry, so both must be cleared — clearing only the flow variable is not enough.

chains.name: GoToCartChain
chains.about: Just a placeholder for navigating to a cart page, since none exists yet

chains.name: RemoveFromCartCancelChain
chains.about: User clicked "No, keep in cart". Close the dialog and force a binding re-evaluation so any checkboxes that were visually unchecked by the user's click reaffirm their checked state from selectedEquipmentKeys.

chains.name: RemoveFromCartConfirmChain
chains.about: User confirmed "Yes, remove from cart". Handles both single-checkbox uncheck and deselect-all, via pendingUncheckEquipmentIds (1+ ids).

chains.name: enforcePageAccessChain
chains.about: Page-level RBAC deep-link guard. GENERATED - every copy is byte-identical; change the template and regenerate rather than editing one copy. Copies exist because a page's eventListeners resolve a bare chain id against that page's OWN <page>-chains folder, so an app-level chain referenced by name 404s. This file holds NO policy: the decision (canEnterPage), the page code (getPageCodeForPage), the redirect target (getRoleHomeTarget) and the same-flow test (isSameFlow) all live in $application.functions. Deriving the page code at runtime is what lets every copy be identical.

chains.name: goToParentChain
chains.about: Cart is DELIBERATELY preserved across this back-navigation: the user is stepping back to amend the request header (dates, address, contact) and expects to return to the catalog with their selections intact. Clearing here forced them to re-pick everything after editing one field. Stale carts are still prevented — CreateRequestInitChain wipes both the flow variable and the draft on a FRESH entry (isReturningToCreate false, e.g. arriving from the dashboard), so a genuinely new request always starts empty. The clear here was redundant for that purpose. The explicit-discard path…

modules.name: draftStorage
modules.about: Returns true if localStorage has a non-empty draft for this key. On resume pages (catalog, cart) we always prefer the persisted draft over whatever VBCS initialized the flow variable to — otherwise default values on the variable (e.g. request.creditLimit) make the variable look "non-empty" and would silently block hydration, dropping user-typed fields like `location` after a refresh.

modules.name: catalogCart
modules.about: Cart helpers, shared by the catalog's add-to-cart pathways. IMPORTANT — staging vs cart are SEPARATE: • STAGING: selectedEquipmentKeys (checkbox highlight) + pendingQtyById ({id: qty}) + pendingRowById ({id: rawRow}). Set by checking a card / changing its stepper. NOT yet in the cart. • CART: CartItemsArray — the real cart, changed ONLY by an explicit Add to Cart / Add Checked / Select-All+Add action, which consumes staging. Under SDP+DPV the equipment rows live in the data provider (not a…

modules.name: currentUser
modules.about: Who is the signed-in user? Resolved from BOTH identity sources, because the app is reached two ways and only one of them is populated in each: published inside Fusion -> ?jwt=... on the URL, decoded for its `sub` dev / Designer preview -> $application.user, populated by VB Neither alone is sufficient. $application.user comes back with empty `login` and `userName` in this environment even while VB logs "User john.dunbar is authenticated"; the JWT is absent on a direct nav, a bookmark or in…

modules.name: templateScope
modules.about: Who may SEE, EDIT and DELETE an equipment request template. Templates used to be one flat, anonymous, permanent list: SaveTemplateChain hard-coded isSharedFlag:'Y' on every save, so all of them were global, and nothing in the UI could ever change or remove one. This module owns the rules that give them a scope and an owner. TWO SCOPES, carried by a column that already existed: IS_SHARED_FLAG = 'Y' GLOBAL everyone sees it; only manager tier edits it IS_SHARED_FLAG = 'N' PERSONAL only its owner…

modules.name: fetchAllPages
modules.about: Read a whole paged list, not just its first page. ASKING FOR A BIG size IS NOT ENOUGH. These endpoints cap the page and return their own maximum without saying so. Verified on the equipment master: 306 rows exist, `size=10000` came back with recordCount=306, pageSize=200, totalPages=2, hasMore=true — a valid HTTP 200 carrying two thirds of the data. Nothing throws, nothing warns; the caller just silently works from a partial set. That truncation has already caused two separate visible bugs: -…

modules.name: catalogCriterion
modules.about: Helpers for merging sidebar selections into the smart-search filterCriterion, so the sidebar and the smart-search chips share one filter state (the DPV applies filterCriterion server-side). Criterion shapes follow oj-smart-search: single chip → { op:'$eq', value:{ field: v } } keyword only → { text, matchBy:'phrase' } combined → { $tag:'_root_', op:'$and', criteria:[...] }

modules.name: orgFilterOptions
modules.about: Org smart-search filter — one definition of the chip, shared by every page that offers it (Equipment Schedule, Equipment Master, Equipment Workbench). WHAT "ORG" IS. The inventory org a unit sits in, taken from BU & Org Mapping rows with ORG_ROLE = 'EQUIPMENT_YARD' (EQR_BU_ORG_MAPPING). That is the whole vocabulary: a BU has ONE list of orgs where its equipment lives, and there is no separate maintenance-org concept in EquipRite — Fusion models an inv-org-to-maint-org link but leaves it NULL…

modules.name: deliveryCoords
modules.about: Resolves the coordinates of the request's DELIVERY ADDRESS, so the catalog can price equipment from the yard nearest to where it is being delivered. There are two ways a delivery address gets onto a request, and this covers both so nearest-yard pricing doesn't silently depend on which one was used: 1. MAP DRAWER ("Enter Delivery location") — the user dropped a pin or picked a geocoder suggestion, so exact coordinates already exist on the page ($page.variables.pickedLat / pickedLng). Preferred…

modules.name: geocoder
modules.about: Mapbox public geocoding token — the app's own token, identical to the one in equipment-schedule-page.js, line-detail-page.js and the two create-request pages. It's a "pk." public token; safe in client code. WAS a leftover Bryntum DEMO token ('matsbryntse'), copied in with their sample map code. That token is not ours and Mapbox rejects it with 401 Unauthorized, so every lookup() silently returned null (the function is best-effort and swallows !resp.ok). Symptom: addresses resolved but…

rest.summary: List all subclasses across every class (flat)
Get Business Unit to Inventory Org mappings

The active EQUIPMENT_YARD org nearest a delivery point. Same resolution views/equipment-catalog already performs internally for nearest-yard pricing, exposed so the catalog's Org chip can be PRE-FILLED with it and the cart's Submit can fall back to it. One org per call, no paging. Returns an empty body when no yard qualifies (no coordinates on the yard master, or none active) - the caller then leaves the chip empty and the backend falls back to the blanket schedule. Requested of the backend 2026-11-05 (docs/EQUIPMENT_REQUESTED_ORG_BACKEND_ASK_2026-11-05.md).
